structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: The text is a letter from Hero MotoCorp to stock exchanges submitting the FY 2024-25 Annual Report and AGM Notice, sent electronically and via website, with a letter for unregistered emails. It announces the 42nd AGM on August 5, 2025, via video conferencing. The Annual Report's contents page covers corporate overview, management discussion, statutory reports, and financial statements. It highlights the company's vision, mission, values, resources, material topics, strategic pillars, risk monitoring, stakeholder value creation, and key financials like earnings per share and new product launches. The summary includes the company's address and contact details.

structure.title: Hero MotoCorp Corporate Overview: Vision, Strategy, and Value Creation
structure.summary: The page presents Hero MotoCorp's corporate overview, beginning with its vision to be the future of mobility and values of passion, integrity, respect, and courage, alongside a mission to create, collaborate, and inspire. It highlights the company's four-decade legacy serving 124 million+ riders through dependable products and a customer-first approach. It details investments in future-ready technologies, R&D, electric mobility, intelligent systems, and digital transformation initiatives like Hero Premia and Hero 2.0. The page outlines strategic focus areas including growing the core, winning in premium, building EV leadership, diversifying revenue, and driving ESG. It covers material topics across environment, social, and governance, key risks, and stakeholder groups, emphasizing consistent value creation.

structure.title: 4 PERFORMANCE HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: The text highlights Hero MotoCorp's performance in FY 2024-25, including financial metrics: Profit After Tax of ₹4,610 crore (16.2% YoY growth), contribution to government exchequer ₹13,525 crore (7.8% YoY), Earnings Per Share ₹231 (16.1% YoY), Revenue ₹40,756 crore (8.8% YoY), EBITDA ₹5,868 crore (11.6% YoY), and 5.9 million units sold, reaffirming its position as the world's largest two-wheeler manufacturer by volume. It also covers operational and strategic developments: 80 new Premia stores at FY exit, 100% OBD2 Phase-B compliance, 12 new product launches (India: 7 ICE, 1 EV; International: 4), total R&D spend of ₹1,039 crore, becoming the first Indian OEM to win the FIM World Rally-Raid Championship, and entry into the Philippines market as part of global expansion.

structure.title: 6 ESG TARGET AND HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: This ESG report highlights Hero MotoCorp's FY 2024-25 progress: environmental targets including 45% progress toward 100% Scope 1 and 2 carbon neutrality by 2030, 100% zero waste to landfill certification with over 99% diversion, 500% water positivity, renewable energy use of 497 lakh kWh and 8.43 kWh per vehicle, freshwater intensity of 0.13 KL per vehicle, 95%+ product recyclability, single-use plastic-free status, and ISO 27001 certification at all manufacturing facilities. Social targets cover 13.2% gender diversity, 102 specially-abled employees, Ride Safe India reaching 2.92 lakh participants, remedial education for 10,554 students, higher education scholarships for 711 students, CSR impacting 8.47 lakh beneficiaries with ₹80.54 crore investment. Governance enhancements include quarterly ESG oversight by the Sustainability and CSR Committee, an expanded Environmental Policy, a comprehensive information security policy, and scaled-up third-party assessments via Sustainable Partner Development and Green Dealership programmes. Additional commitments: 30% green dealerships by 2030, 30% gender diversity by 2030, and 95%+ product recyclability achieved in 2025.

structure.title: 8 EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
structure.summary: The Executive Chairman's message begins with a patriotic 'Nation First' theme, celebrating India's rise and Hero MotoCorp's role in mobility and nation-building. It honors founder Dr. Brijmohan Lall Munjal's legacy. The message highlights India's economic progress under PM Modi, citing IMF GDP growth forecasts of 6.2% and 6.3%, and reforms like PM Gati Shakti, PLI, and Digital India. It notes Hero's 24-year leadership as the world's largest two-wheeler manufacturer, with 124 million customers in 48 countries and 5.9 million vehicles delivered in its 41st year, reflecting strong financials and commitment to Viksit Bharat. It also references external data on EV sales growth by 2030 and India's electric 3-wheeler market leadership.

structure.title: 10 EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
structure.summary: The Executive Chairman's message highlights Hero MotoCorp's values-driven culture, performance and purpose-led organization, and global recognitions including TIME's World's Best Companies and Best Companies in Asia-Pacific 2025, plus ET NOW's Best Organisations for Women. It covers innovation investments in India's startup ecosystem, electric mobility advancements with VIDA's 200% sales surge, VIDA V2, VIDA Acro's Red Dot Award, global expansion into Germany, France, Spain, and the UK, partnerships with Ather Energy, Euler Motors, and Zero Motorcycles. It details FY 2024-25 product launches across premium, scooter, and legacy segments, international market growth of 43% YoY, entry into Europe, and sustainability efforts achieving 500% water positivity.

structure.title: 12 EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
structure.summary: The Executive Chairman's message highlights sustainability achievements: 95% product recyclability surpassing AIS 129 benchmark, 45% carbon neutrality, 30% channel partners adopting Green Dealership practices with 7.1 MWp solar capacity, and inclusion in DJSI World and Emerging Markets. It covers people initiatives for women representation and the Gurugram facility's Sword of Honour. CSR under 'Hero We Care' touched 847,000 lives through road safety (300,000 beneficiaries), education, mobile medical units (120,000 beneficiaries), veteran support, and Project Saksham empowering 4,000 women. Sports initiatives include Paralympic partnerships, Hero MotoSports' FIM Rally-Raid World Championship win, FIH hockey partnership, and Hero World Challenge golf. The message concludes with thanks and a forward-looking vision.

structure.title: 14 MESSAGE FROM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR AND ACTING CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER
structure.summary: The Executive Director and Acting CEO reflects on Hero MotoCorp's 24-year market leadership, record revenue and profit, and momentum into the 25th year. He outlines favorable macroeconomic tailwinds, a new dual reporting format for wholesale and VAHAN registrations, rising retail market share, 65% retail finance penetration, and calibrated inventory. The company is intensifying focus on the 125cc segment with the Xtreme 125R and Glamour, advancing premiumization with the Xtreme 250R, Xpulse 210, and Harley-Davidson X440, and launching scooters like Destini 125 and Xoom 125. It is expanding premium retail with 80 Premia stores and upgrading 90% of dealerships to Hero 2.0. VIDA EV sales grew around 200% with the mass-segment VIDA V2, 4,000 fast charging points, 500 service centres, and plans for the VX2 with battery-as-a-service. Global exports grew over 40% under an 80-20 strategy, with premium products at nearly 40% of global sales. The PAM business achieved record revenue of ₹5,828 crore, up 8%. The company acquired a stake in Euler Motors to enter electric three-wheelers. ESG progress includes achieving three of six sustainability goals, inventorying over 95% of Scope 3 emissions, and conducting a biodiversity risk assessment. The Surge S32 won TIME’s 100 Best Innovations of 2024, Red Dot: Best of the Best, and A’Design Platinum. The CEO commits to accelerating growth, expanding electric mobility, premium play, core segment value, international presence, and long-term stakeholder value under the mission to 'leap ahead with purpose'.

nodes.title: 3.20Contingent liabilities and contingent assets
nodes.summary:
3.20Contingent liabilities and contingent assets
A contingent liability exists when there is a possible but not probable obligation, or a present obligation that may, but probably will not, require an outflow of resources, or a present obligation whose amount cannot be estimated reliably. Contingent liabilities do not warrant provisions, but are disclosed unless the possibility of outflow of resources is remote. Contingent assets are neither recognised nor disclosed in the standalone financial statements. However, contingent assets are assessed continually and if it is virtually certain that an inflow of economic benefits will arise, the asset and related income are recognised in the period in which the change occurs.

Goel & Co. as Cost Auditors for FY 2025-26 at a remuneration of Rs. 3,30,000 plus taxes, requiring member ratification; appointment of M/s SGS Associates LLP as Secretarial Auditors for a five-year term from FY 2025-26 at a fee of Rs. 4.5 lakh plus taxes, with details of their eligibility and firm profile; and re-appointment of ACM Birender Singh Dhanoa (Retd.) as an Independent Director for a second term of five years from October 1, 2025, highlighting his qualifications, experience, and board involvement. It also includes Annexure A with details of directors seeking appointment/re-appointment, including Ms. Vasudha Dinodia and ACM Dhanoa, covering their resumes, qualifications, experience, remuneration, shareholding, relationships, and committee memberships.
